title: EMA/CO for gestational trophoblastic neoplasia
context_label: High-risk or resistant gestational trophoblastic neoplasia
schedule_label: Two treatment days in week one, oral rescue, then two different IV medicines on day 8.
schedule_summary: Dactinomycin and etoposide are followed by methotrexate over 12 hours. Write down the infusion start time so you know when rescue begins. Return for dactinomycin and etoposide. Oral folinic acid starts today. The day 1 and 2 anti-sickness medicines form one course. Start the first oral folinic acid tablet 24 hours after the methotrexate infusion STARTS. Take four doses 12 hours apart unless your team gives you a different written rescue plan. If a tablet is late, missed or vomited, phone the unit straight away. Vincristine is given only into a vein, followed by cyclophosphamide. Tell the team about constipation or numbness before treatment. The full sequence repeats every 14 days.
purpose: Treat the trophoblastic tumour with the aim of cure. Serial blood hCG measures how the disease responds.
indication_text: High-risk GTN (FIGO score 7 or above), low-risk disease after failure or relapse following sequential single-agent therapy, or low-risk disease after methotrexate failure with hCG above 1,000 IU/L.
administration_text: Dactinomycin and etoposide are followed by methotrexate over 12 hours. Write down the infusion start time so you know when rescue begins. Return for dactinomycin and etoposide. Oral folinic acid starts today. The day 1 and 2 anti-sickness medicines form one course. Start the first oral folinic acid tablet 24 hours after the methotrexate infusion STARTS. Take four doses 12 hours apart unless your team gives you a different written rescue plan. If a tablet is late, missed or vomited, phone the unit straight away. Vincristine is given only into a vein, followed by cyclophosphamide. Tell the team about constipation or numbness before treatment. The full sequence repeats every 14 days.
monitoring_summary: Repeat blood count, kidney and liver tests. Check serum hCG on day 1, more often if indicated.
review_status: Feasibility build. Clinical, pharmacy and patient review pending.

agents.name: Dactinomycin
agents.explanation: Interferes with the way tumour cells use DNA to make RNA.
agents.mechanism: Interferes with the way tumour cells use DNA to make RNA.
agents.watch: Tell the nurse immediately if the injection site burns or stings.
visual: Interferes with the way tumour cells use DNA to make RNA.

agents.name: Etoposide
agents.explanation: Prevents tumour cells repairing DNA during division.
agents.mechanism: Prevents tumour cells repairing DNA during division.
agents.watch: Tell the nurse if you feel faint or breathless during the infusion.
visual: Prevents tumour cells repairing DNA during division.

agents.name: Methotrexate
agents.explanation: Prevents rapidly dividing trophoblastic cells using folate to make new DNA.
agents.mechanism: Prevents rapidly dividing trophoblastic cells using folate to make new DNA.
agents.watch: Check new medicines with oncology pharmacy and follow the timed rescue plan.
visual: Prevents rapidly dividing trophoblastic cells using folate to make new DNA.

agents.name: Folinic acid
agents.explanation: Supplies a usable form of folate to protect healthy cells after methotrexate.
agents.mechanism: Supplies a usable form of folate to protect healthy cells after methotrexate.
agents.watch: Ring the unit for any missed, late or vomited rescue dose.
visual: Supplies a usable form of folate to protect healthy cells after methotrexate.

agents.name: Vincristine
agents.explanation: Interferes with the structures that cells use to divide.
agents.mechanism: Interferes with the structures that cells use to divide.
agents.watch: Report tingling, weakness or severe constipation. This medicine is for IV use only.
visual: Interferes with the structures that cells use to divide.

agents.name: Cyclophosphamide
agents.explanation: Damages DNA so tumour cells cannot keep dividing.
agents.mechanism: Damages DNA so tumour cells cannot keep dividing.
agents.watch: Tell the team about painful urination or blood in your urine.
visual: Damages DNA so tumour cells cannot keep dividing.

common_effects.title: How you feel between visits
common_effects.text: Tiredness, nausea or appetite changes can make everyday activities harder. Ask your team for help if symptoms interfere with eating or drinking.

serious_effects.title: IV site injury · Dactinomycin
serious_effects.text: Report pain, swelling or blistering at the injection site immediately.

serious_effects.title: Sore mouth · Dactinomycin
serious_effects.text: Phone if mouth ulcers prevent you drinking.

serious_effects.title: Infection or bleeding · Dactinomycin
serious_effects.text: Contact the unit urgently for fever, chills or unusual bleeding.

serious_effects.title: Low blood counts · Etoposide
serious_effects.text: Phone urgently for fever, chills or unexplained bleeding.

serious_effects.title: Infusion reaction · Etoposide
serious_effects.text: Tell the nurse immediately about flushing, faintness or breathing problems.

serious_effects.title: Mouth ulcers · Methotrexate
serious_effects.text: Ask for advice if sores make eating or drinking difficult.

serious_effects.title: Slower clearance · Methotrexate
serious_effects.text: Attend kidney blood tests. Report vomiting or difficulty drinking.

serious_effects.title: Rescue tablets · Folinic acid
serious_effects.text: Check each time against your written schedule. Phone about a missed or vomited dose.

serious_effects.title: Nerve changes · Vincristine
serious_effects.text: Report numbness, tingling or weakness before treatment.

serious_effects.title: Constipation · Vincristine
serious_effects.text: Phone urgently for severe abdominal pain, swelling or inability to pass stool.

serious_effects.title: Bladder irritation · Cyclophosphamide
serious_effects.text: Report blood in the urine, pain or difficulty passing urine.

serious_effects.title: Low blood counts · Cyclophosphamide
serious_effects.text: Phone urgently for fever, chills or unexpected bleeding.

questions.q: What happens at my next visit?
questions.a: Two treatment days in week one, oral rescue, then two different IV medicines on day 8.

questions.q: Which symptoms should I phone about?
questions.a: Call your oncology unit urgently for fever, shaking chills or sudden illness. Call for severe constipation, abdominal pain, weakness, or a missed folinic acid dose. Report stinging at an IV site immediately.

questions.q: What should I plan before starting?
questions.a: Bring your medicines list and your GTN centre contact details.
After remission your specialist arranges hCG every two weeks for six months, then monthly for six months, then every two months for two years.

questions.q: Why are there more cycles after hCG returns to normal?
questions.a: Treatment continues to clear disease too small to detect. Low-risk disease usually needs three more courses. With high-risk disease the usual plan is three more cycles (six weeks), or four (eight weeks) with adverse features such as liver metastases.

questions.q: Should I call about a dry cough between visits?
questions.a: Phone your 24-hour oncology number straight away for a persistent dry cough or new breathlessness. Methotrexate can cause lung inflammation, and infection can cause similar symptoms. Your team needs to assess you even if you have no fever.

evidence.title: EMA/CO in 272 patients with high-risk disease
evidence.interpretation: Long-term follow-up documents responses and outcomes with EMA/CO in high-risk GTN.
evidence.limitations: Single-centre cohort including previously treated patients.

monitoring_schedule.title: Tests and timing

rows.label: Before treatment
cells: Check blood count, kidney and liver function and serum hCG using a validated assay.
Bring your medicines list and your GTN centre contact details.

rows.label: Before each cycle
cells: Repeat blood count, kidney and liver tests. Check serum hCG on day 1, more often if indicated.
Ask how your hCG trend affects the next treatment.

rows.label: After treatment
cells: Continue follow-up through your GTN service.
After remission your specialist arranges hCG every two weeks for six months, then monthly for six months, then every two months for two years.

monitoring_schedule.note: Scan dates and tumour-marker testing are individualised by your oncology team.
